subject: Recess and Wellness Policy Revisions
overview: The subcommittee met with administrators and parents to discuss updating the district wellness policy to protect K-8 recess, specifically regarding duration, weather consistency, and disciplinary restrictions.

items.title: Review of Wellness Policy ADF
items.summary: The subcommittee convened to fulfill a May 16, 2022, mandate to revise the wellness policy to ensure daily unrestricted free play for K-8 students.

items.title: District Recess Overview
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent and various principals described current recess practices, noting elementary students typically receive 20 to 30 minutes daily while middle schoolers receive approximately 20 minutes.

items.title: Defining Child-Directed Play
items.summary: Public commenters and committee members discussed defining recess as 'child-directed play' and advocated for prohibiting the use of screens during indoor recess.

items.title: Recess as Discipline
items.summary: The chair noted that Medford's current policy does not mention recess, whereas neighboring districts explicitly prohibit withholding it as a form of discipline.

items.title: Consistency and Weather Standards
items.summary: Committee members highlighted parental concerns regarding inconsistent weather-related indoor recess decisions across different schools and the need for a uniform 'real feel' temperature threshold.

items.title: Logical Consequences and Safety
items.summary: Administrators discussed using 'logical consequences' for unsafe behavior, such as shadowing a teacher or walking laps, while some members expressed concern that such practices can lead to public shaming and lack data tracking.

items.title: Next Steps and Policy Drafting
items.summary: The chair outlined plans for a future meeting to draft language for the wellness policy regarding definitions of play, weather consistency, and limits on using recess for disciplinary purposes.
